reason: The septum should separate the heart’s two sides, preparing the pump for its distinct routes. It is also the only offered action.
expectation: I expect a heart with separate right and left sides, still needing valves and connections.

effect: The heart is now divided, and its two marked slots make the valve-fitting goal clear.
reaction: The comparison showing backward flow gives the valves a clear purpose.
reason: I'll fit the inlet valves to one of the marked positions.
expectation: I expect the ventricular inlets to be fitted, with the outlets still empty.

alternatives.reason: The outlet valves are also needed, but I chose to start with the inlets.

effect: The inlet valves are fitted, and their role in preventing backward flow during a squeeze is clear.
reaction: The open and closed views make their function easy to follow.
reason: The outlet valves fill the remaining slot and are the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the outlet valves to be fitted, completing both valve sets.

effect: Both valve sets are fitted, and the outlet valves prevent blood returning from the arteries between beats.
reaction: The distinction between the inlet and outlet valves is clear.
reason: Conducting tissue is the only offered combination and should help coordinate the heart’s contractions.
expectation: I expect the heart to gain electrical pathways that coordinate its beats.

effect: The conducting tissue gives the heart a timed electrical sequence, with the atria contracting before the ventricles.
reaction: The matching electrical and squeeze arrows make the coordination clear.
reason: The pulmonary loop is the only offered combination and should connect the heart to the lungs.
expectation: I expect a route from the right side of the heart through the lungs and back to the left side.

effect: The pulmonary route now connects the right heart to the lungs and returns to the left atrium; the route to body tissues remains open.
reaction: The separate routes are becoming easier to follow.
reason: The systemic vessel network should connect the heart to body tissues, and it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the body’s vessel network to connect to the heart, forming a route through tissues and back.

effect: The heart now has separate pulmonary and systemic loops, forming the circulation frame.
reaction: Connecting the two routes makes the overall layout clearer.
reason: The heart’s own vessels should supply its muscle, and this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect coronary vessels to be added to the circulation frame.

effect: The heart muscle now has its own blood supply connected to the circulation, distinct from blood in its chambers.
reaction: The explanation that the pump needs its own supply makes this connection meaningful.
reason: Adding blood should complete the connected circulation, and it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect blood to enter the connected pulmonary, systemic and coronary routes.

effect: Adding blood completed the circulation and clarified the sequence from right heart to lungs, left heart, body, and back.
reaction: Seeing the routes joined into one circulation was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the heart’s own vessels was most worthwhile: it explained why the heart muscle needs a blood supply separate from the blood in its chambers.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the conducting tissue felt less engaging because it was the only offered combination, and the result mostly confirmed what I expected.

surprise.text: The coronary connection made me think about the heart as tissue that needs supplying, as well as a pump.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although most decisions offered only one combination, so there was little choice to reason through.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how circulation supports the responsive arm, though I would hope for more meaningful choices. The described diagrams and brief explanations made the routes understandable, but I cannot assess whether finished illustrations would be clear.
